Fact checks›Roads & impact fees

The claim

A $5.5 million gift was spent on a road

“QTS gave 5.5 million dollars to help citizens and the mayor decided to use those funds to fix a road.”

Seen: Eagle Mountain City Tax Referendum Facebook group, August 2026.

Our finding Not accurate

The record contradicts it.

There was no $5.5 million gift. Two figures spoken on the same night have been fused: QTS agreed to pay the roughly $5 million cost of widening Pony Express Parkway, and $5,591,594 was the new revenue from the tax rate the council adopted hours later.

The numbers

QTS road commitmentwidening plus two traffic signals≈$5,000,000
Revenue from the 0.001500 rate+183.02% · repealed 12 days later$5,591,594
Corridor projectMAG regional funding, not the city levy$11,400,000

What’s true

QTS did commit money, and the mayor did ask for it. On August 6 Mayor Gray told the hearing that the city had been trying to work out how to widen Pony Express Parkway, that he phoned QTS to propose a reimbursement agreement, and that they came back offering to pay the entire bill rather than the half he had asked for.

Where it goes wrong

It was road money in the sentence it was first mentioned. There were never general funds sitting there to be redirected. And the $5.5 million in circulation is a different number from the same meeting: the net revenue above the certified rate that a rate of 0.001500 would raise, $5,591,594, which finance staff computed during the deliberation and which was read into the adopting motion. That rate was repealed twelve days later.

More detail

The mayor's stated reason for making the call is the same argument the post makes: that traffic generated by the data center's workers should not be a burden carried by residents.

The wider corridor work is not city property tax either. The Ranches Parkway and Pony Express project discussed on August 4 runs on MAG regional funding, with the city cash-flowing parts of it against a reimbursement interlocal. Staff put the design and construction at $11.4 million that night, and the programmed figure at $11.8 million in current dollars, $13.8 million as MAG budgets it for 2030.

Where this comes from

Every finding here is drawn from an open-meeting recording or a published document. Check it yourself.
